insights.title: Sleep Duration & Afternoon Migraine Correlation
insights.observation: Vestibular migraines occurred on 4 out of 5 days where night sleep was under 6.2 hours.
insights.detailedAnalysis: Across 14 tracked days, days with <6.2h sleep showed an average next-day pain rating of 6.6/10 compared to 2.1/10 on days with >7.5h sleep. The onset typically manifests between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM, preceded by neck tightness.
insights.actionableSuggestion: Explore buffering your evening wind-down starting at 20:45 to safeguard a consistent 7.5h sleep window before busy work days.
insights.nonClinicalNote: This is an observed statistical pattern in your personal records, not a diagnostic medical finding.

insights.title: Cognitive Duration Impact on Energy Depletion
insights.observation: Continuous cognitive tasks exceeding 45 minutes lead to a 3.0 point average drop in energy.
insights.detailedAnalysis: When writing or reviewing data for longer than 45 minutes without an intermediate rest stop, post-activity energy dropped by an average of 3.0 points and required 45 minutes of horizontal recovery. In contrast, 25-minute Pomodoro pacing kept energy steady.
insights.actionableSuggestion: Setting a quiet 25-minute chime during laptop work may protect your afternoon reserve spoons.
insights.nonClinicalNote: Pacing strategies are personalized self-management tools and do not substitute for clinical advice.

insights.title: Consistent Magnesium Adherence & Evening Muscle Relaxation
insights.observation: Nighttime neck and trapezius stiffness ratings declined by 40% on weeks with 100% magnesium adherence.
insights.detailedAnalysis: You have taken your Magnesium Glycinate 13 out of the past 14 days at bedtime. On days where it was taken with herbal tea, morning stiffness duration dropped from 90 minutes to under 30 minutes.
insights.actionableSuggestion: Continue your evening ritual as scheduled; keep noting any subtle digestive tolerance.
insights.nonClinicalNote: Report observed medication responses to your prescribing physician during follow-ups.

communityPosts.title: How I learned to stop feeling guilty about 20-minute horizontal rest
communityPosts.body: For years with fibromyalgia and POTS, I thought resting meant "giving up" on my day. Morrow's pacing logs showed me clearly that a 20-minute dark-room eye break at 1:30 PM actually saves my entire evening. When you pace proactively before the crash hits, it is not lost time—it is maintenance.

comments.content: This resonated so deeply. Preemptive rest is completely different from collapse rest!
Thank you for this reminder today. I was just about to push through a headache.

communityPosts.title: What questions helped you most when speaking to a neurologist about migraines?
communityPosts.body: I am preparing my 30-day symptom report for an appointment next Tuesday. In the past I would get flustered and forget details. Printing out the frequency trends and trigger logs has already given me so much calm. What specific questions helped you get taken seriously?

comments.content: Focus on functional impairment rather than just pain score: e.g. "On 4 days this month, light sensitivity made it impossible to look at screens for 3 hours."

communityPosts.title: Gentle wins of the week: sharing small victories that healthy people might miss
communityPosts.body: Made my own bone broth soup today and did 10 minutes of somatic vagus nerve breathing without triggering dizziness. What is one small, tender win you are celebrating in your body this week?
